To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SCH 40120 is metabolized in vitro by the liver of rat, dog, cyno‐molgus monkey, and man to the corresponding 6,7, and 9 carbinols and the 6 ketone.
SCH 40120 was hydroxylated at the cyclohexenol ring in the rat, dog, cyno‐mologus monkey and human, and that the resulting carbinols were glucuroni‐dated in all species.
SCH 40120 was metabolized to the 6‐,7‐, and9‐carbinol metabolites in rat, dog, cyno‐ molgus monkey, and in human liver slices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structure elucidation and in vitro metabolism of SCH 40020 and its derivatives.
the development of novel antitumor agents based on the use of the natural product taxol.
the development of a novel class of antitumor agents, the pyridopyridines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolism of SCH 40020 in vitro in the liver slices of the four species was qualitatively similar, with the major metabolites being the 6‐ and 9‐hydroxy and 6‐ketones.
the metabolism of SCH 40210, a potent topical antipsoriactic agent, in vitro in the four species studied is very similar, but not identical.
the metabolism of SCH 40020 is similar in all four species, and that the major pathway is the oxidation of the aliphatic ring to form the 9‐carbonyl, followed by conjugation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the major pathway for the metabolism of the drug in all four species studied was hydroxylation of the aliphatic ring followed by conjugation of the carbinol with glucuronic acid.
SCH 40120 was metabolized by the liver to 6‐,7‐ and 9‐hydroxylated metabolites, the glucuronides of the 6 and 9‐OH metabolites, and the 9‐keto‐6‐hydroxy metabolite.
the major route of SCH 40110 metabolism in rat, dog, cyno‐ molgus monkey, and humans is hydroxylation at the cyclohexenol ring and conjugation of the carbinol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver slices can be used for in vitro metabolism studies of SCH 4012.0.
the in vitro metabolic profile of SCH 4012O is similar to the metabolic profile in vivo.
we have shown that the liver is a major site of drug metabolism, and that we have developed a method for studying drug metabolism in the liver.
